meta.review_notes: Android analysis shares the same privacy policy as iOS. No material platform-specific differences were found in the policy text. Policy date shows January 2021 but current page references newer features (Meta AI, Channels, Accounts Center). The policy date may not reflect incremental amendments. Significant data-sharing with Meta Companies for cross-platform advertising is the primary concern. Financial/payment data practices for markets like India (WhatsApp Pay) are deferred to a separate payments privacy policy not analyzed here.

app.name: WhatsApp Messenger
app.description: A free, end-to-end encrypted messaging and calling app used by over 2 billion people worldwide, owned by Meta.

verdict.one_liner: World-class encryption on your messages, but WhatsApp feeds your contacts, behavior, and device data into Meta's advertising machine.
verdict.summary: WhatsApp uses genuine end-to-end encryption so your actual message content is private, and it does not show third-party banner ads inside the app. However, it regularly uploads your entire phone contact list to its servers, collects extensive device fingerprinting data, and explicitly shares behavioral and usage information with Facebook, Instagram, and other Meta companies to improve ads and products across those platforms. You are not the advertiser's customer here—you are the data source.
verdict.recommendation_reason: The encryption is real and valuable, but the scope of metadata and behavioral data flowing to Meta's advertising ecosystem is substantial and largely non-negotiable for non-EU users. Consider Signal as a privacy-first alternative if this concerns you.

red.title: Your entire address book is uploaded to Meta servers
red.plain_english: WhatsApp regularly uploads all the phone numbers in your contacts—even people who don't use WhatsApp—to its servers. Meta can then see your social network even if those people never agreed to it.

red.title: Your behavior powers ads on Facebook and Instagram
red.plain_english: WhatsApp explicitly states it shares your usage data with Meta companies to improve 'ads and products experience' across Facebook, Instagram, and other Meta apps. So using WhatsApp makes you a better ad target on other Meta platforms.

red.title: Deep device fingerprinting linked across all Meta products
red.plain_english: WhatsApp collects your phone model, battery level, signal strength, network carrier, IP address, and unique device identifiers — and ties all of this to your identity across every Meta app you use.

red.title: Your rough location is always inferred from your IP
red.plain_english: Even if you never share your GPS location, WhatsApp always calculates approximately where you are using your IP address and phone number area code.

red.title: No real opt-out from Meta data sharing for most users
red.plain_english: Unless you are in the EU or UK (where GDPR gives you more rights), there is no meaningful way to use WhatsApp without your data feeding into Meta's advertising system.

green.title: End-to-end encryption on all messages and calls
green.plain_english: WhatsApp cannot read your messages or listen to your calls. The content of your conversations is encrypted so only you and the person you're talking to can see it.

green.title: Messages are not stored on WhatsApp servers
green.plain_english: Once a message is delivered, it is deleted from WhatsApp's servers. Undelivered messages are kept for up to 30 days only, then deleted.

green.title: No third-party banner ads inside the app
green.plain_english: WhatsApp does not display ads from outside advertisers inside the chat interface. This is a firm policy commitment stated in both the ToS and Privacy Policy.

green.title: You can fully delete your account and data
green.plain_english: WhatsApp provides a built-in 'Delete My Account' feature that wipes your account data, removes you from groups, and deletes undelivered messages from servers.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp only uses your camera and microphone when you actively make a call or record a voice/video message. It does not listen in the background.
categories.detail: Camera and microphone access is on-demand and directly tied to core features: voice calls, video calls, sending voice messages, and taking photos or videos to share. There is no indication of background access, and media sent is protected by end-to-end encryption in transit.
categories.policy_excerpt: Core messaging and calling services require microphone and camera access at the time of use, with encryption applied in transit.
concerns: No specific statement explicitly ruling out background microphone access in the policy text

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Your exact GPS location is only shared if you choose to use the location-sharing feature. However, WhatsApp always estimates roughly where you are using your IP address and phone number, even if you never touch the location feature.
categories.detail: Precise location requires explicit user permission and is used only when the user actively shares their location with a contact. However, a passive approximate location (city/country level) is always inferred from the user's IP address and phone number area code, with no opt-out available. This passive inference is used for diagnostics and unspecified additional purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: Even without using location-related features, the app uses IP addresses and phone number area codes to calculate approximate location for diagnostic and other purposes.
concerns: Passive IP-based location inference is always on with no opt-out
Inferred location data flows to Meta Companies

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp uploads all the phone numbers in your address book to its servers on a regular basis. This includes numbers of people who have never agreed to share their information with WhatsApp. While WhatsApp says it protects non-users' data, your full contact graph is known to Meta.
categories.detail: The policy explicitly states that users 'can' provide phone numbers from their mobile address book 'on a regular basis.' In practice, this is the primary mechanism for finding other WhatsApp users and is treated as a core function. Non-user contact numbers are handled with some protective measures per the policy, but the full social graph is uploaded and retained by WhatsApp/Meta. There is no technical indication that this data is isolated from Meta's broader data infrastructure.
categories.policy_excerpt: Users may provide phone numbers from their mobile address book on a regular basis, including numbers of both WhatsApp users and other contacts.
concerns: Non-users' phone numbers are uploaded without their consent
Regular (ongoing) upload, not a one-time action
Social graph data is particularly valuable for Meta's advertising targeting
Policy does not explicitly exclude contact data from Meta-wide data sharing

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp only accesses your photos, videos, and files when you deliberately choose to share them in a conversation. It does not scan your storage in the background.
categories.detail: File and media access is entirely user-initiated for the purpose of sending media in conversations. There is no indication of broad library scanning or background file access. Media sent is end-to-end encrypted in transit and deleted from servers once delivered.
categories.policy_excerpt: Users initiate media sharing; forwarded media is temporarily stored encrypted on servers solely to improve delivery efficiency.

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp shares your data with Facebook, Instagram, and all other Meta companies. This data is used to improve ads and recommendations across those platforms. They also share data with technical service providers. Your data does not appear to be sold to external data brokers, but it extensively powers Meta's advertising ecosystem.
categories.detail: WhatsApp is part of the Meta Companies family and explicitly shares information across that family including for improving 'ads and products experience across Meta Company Products.' Third-party service providers also receive data for infrastructure, analytics, security, and customer support purposes. The policy requires these providers to use data per WhatsApp's instructions, but the Meta intra-family sharing for advertising is the primary concern and covers behavioral, device, account, and usage data.
categories.policy_excerpt: As part of the Meta Companies, WhatsApp shares information with those companies to improve ads and products experience across Meta Company Products.
concerns: Data is used to improve ad targeting on Facebook and Instagram
No meaningful opt-out for non-EU/UK users
Scope of intra-Meta data sharing is broad and not granularly defined
Third-party service providers receive data, though with contractual use restrictions

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: You must give WhatsApp your real phone number to use the app — anonymous use is not possible. Your phone number, name, and profile photo are shared with anyone using the app, and your account can be linked to your Facebook profile via Meta's Accounts Center.
categories.detail: A verified mobile phone number is mandatory for account creation — there is no anonymous use option. Profile name and picture are visible to other users by default. The Terms and policy reference integration with Meta's Accounts Center, allowing your WhatsApp account to be linked to your Facebook and Instagram accounts, creating a unified identity profile that powers targeted advertising across all Meta platforms.
categories.policy_excerpt: Users must provide their mobile phone number to create an account. Accounts can be connected to Meta's Accounts Center for cross-platform integration.
concerns: Real phone number required — no pseudonymous or anonymous use
Account linkable to Facebook/Instagram for unified ad profile
Profile info (name, photo, last seen) visible to any WhatsApp user by default

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp does not show ads inside the app, which is genuinely good. But it does track how you use the app — which features you use, how often, when — and shares this with Meta to make ads better on Facebook and Instagram. You are being tracked; you just don't see the ads in WhatsApp itself.
categories.detail: The policy explicitly states no third-party banner ads within the app, which is accurate. However, behavioral data including feature usage, interaction patterns, frequency and duration of activity, profile updates, and connection patterns is collected and shared with Meta Companies to 'improve your ads and products experience' on other Meta platforms. This constitutes cross-app behavioral tracking, albeit within a corporate family rather than to external ad networks. Non-EU/UK users have no practical opt-out.
categories.policy_excerpt: WhatsApp does not permit third-party banner ads in its Services but shares usage and behavioral data with Meta Companies to improve ads and products experience across those platforms.
concerns: Cross-platform behavioral profiling within Meta ecosystem
No opt-out for non-EU/UK users
Usage patterns, interaction frequency, and feature engagement are all tracked
Data feeds Facebook and Instagram ad targeting even without using those apps

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp says you must be at least 13 to use the app (higher in some countries). There is a parent-managed account option for younger teens. However, the app doesn't verify your age — it just asks you to agree to the terms.
categories.detail: The ToS requires users to be at least 13 years old (or the higher minimum age required in their country). A parent-managed account feature is mentioned for children below the minimum age. However, there is no age verification mechanism beyond self-attestation. Given the app's design is not child-directed, this is a standard approach rather than a major violation, but the lack of enforcement is a mild concern.
categories.policy_excerpt: Users must be at least 13 years old to register and use WhatsApp independently; parent-managed accounts are available where supported.
concerns: No age verification mechanism — self-attestation only
Parent-managed account feature availability varies by country

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp logs your IP address and uses it to estimate where you are in the world — even when you're not using any location features. This happens every time you use the app.
categories.detail: IP address logging is continuous during app use and is explicitly described as being used for location inference (city and country level) and diagnostic purposes. The policy does not restrict this inferred location data from flowing to Meta Companies. Standard connection metadata (online/offline status, last seen, connection type) is also collected and shared with contacts per account settings.
categories.policy_excerpt: IP addresses and phone number area codes are used to calculate approximate location (city and country) for diagnostic and other purposes, even without explicit location feature use.
concerns: IP-based location inference is always on with no opt-out
Connection metadata (online status, last seen) is collected and shared with contacts

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp collects a very detailed picture of your phone: the model, operating system, battery level, signal strength, network carrier, app version, language, timezone, and unique device IDs. Crucially, these device IDs are shared with other Meta apps, so WhatsApp knows this is your same device as the one running Facebook or Instagram.
categories.detail: The policy enumerates an extensive list of device data collected: hardware model, OS information, battery level, signal strength, app version, browser information, mobile network, connection information including phone number and carrier/ISP, language and timezone, IP address, device operation information, and — critically — 'unique identifiers for Meta Company Products associated with the same device or account.' This last item explicitly enables cross-app device linking across the Meta ecosystem for advertising and targeting purposes.
categories.policy_excerpt: Device data collected includes hardware model, OS, battery level, signal strength, carrier, IP, and unique identifiers for Meta Company Products associated with the same device or account.
concerns: Device IDs explicitly linked across all Meta products on the same device
Battery level and signal strength collection goes beyond what is needed for service operation
Enables re-identification even if users have separate accounts on different Meta apps

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp does not collect any health data. If you use fingerprint or face unlock to open the app, that biometric data stays on your phone and is handled by Android — WhatsApp never sees it.
categories.detail: No health or biometric data collection is mentioned or implied in the privacy policy or terms of service. Device-level biometric authentication (fingerprint, face unlock) is a local OS-level function and is not accessed by WhatsApp itself.
categories.policy_excerpt: No health or biometric data collection described in the policy.

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: WhatsApp has a payment feature in some countries (like India). If you use it, they collect payment and transaction details. For users who don't use payments, this doesn't apply. The full payment privacy practices are covered in a separate policy not analyzed here.
categories.detail: Payment services are an optional feature available in select markets (including India, Brazil). If used, the policy states that additional data is processed including 'payment account and transaction data' and information needed to complete the transaction. The policy defers detailed payment privacy practices to a separate payments privacy policy, which was not reviewed in this analysis. The core messaging app does not require payment information.
categories.policy_excerpt: If payment services are used, additional data including payment account and transaction data is processed; full practices are detailed in a separate payments privacy policy.
concerns: Separate payments privacy policy not analyzed — full practices unknown
Payment data collection and retention practices not fully disclosed in main policy

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can delete your WhatsApp account at any time from within the app, and it will wipe your profile data and remove you from groups. However, it won't delete copies of messages that other people have saved, and some data may be kept for legal or safety reasons. You can also download a copy of your data.
categories.detail: WhatsApp provides an in-app 'Delete My Account' feature that removes account data and undelivered messages from servers. A data portability feature ('Request Account Info') is available. However, the policy notes that deleted data may be retained for legal compliance, safety, or integrity purposes. Account deletion does not affect data held by other users (e.g., screenshots, message copies), nor data related to groups the user created. If the app is simply uninstalled without using the deletion feature, data is retained.
categories.policy_excerpt: Account deletion removes profile data and undelivered messages from servers; some data may be retained for legal, security, or integrity purposes.
concerns: Data held by other users (screenshots, message copies) is not deletable
Group data created by the user persists after deletion
Some retention for legal/safety purposes is not time-limited in the policy
Uninstalling without using 'Delete Account' does not delete server-side data

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: If WhatsApp changes its privacy policy, it will notify you and update the effective date. But by continuing to use the app after being notified, you are automatically considered to have accepted the new terms — you don't have to actively agree.
categories.detail: The Terms state that WhatsApp will provide notice of material amendments and update the effective date. However, continued use of the service constitutes acceptance of updated terms. Users who disagree must delete their account. There is no mechanism for selectively accepting or rejecting specific changes, and no requirement for active re-consent beyond notification.
categories.policy_excerpt: WhatsApp will notify users of material policy changes; continued use of the service constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.
concerns: Passive acceptance by continued use — no active re-consent required
No granular opt-out for specific policy changes
